>>264337825
>what other animal has the prospect to become a literal god through gene editing?
No animal has this prospect, including the human mammal. Once gene-editing goes into full swing, the human mammal will eventually be long gone, not to mention the utterly catastrophic socioeconomic consequences. Thinking long-term here, of course. 

You MAY call that evolution, and you'd be right, but some anons want to live (and die) as humans in a Wild world. 

You may want to see paragraphs 122, 170 and 174 of ISAIF for a more eloquent response to the gene-editing question. 

>why not use the potential of the only animal that has figured out the inner workings of the world rather than been its hopeless captive?
Agreed 110%. THIS is EXACTLY why Technique has to go and never come back. 

>to me surrogate activities are necessary.
Not just you, this is true for ALL humans except maybe the pooprest of the poor in 'developing' nations who don't have the time, inclination for anything other than their day-to-day miserable existence as the true peasants of technological civilization.
>after a European explorer met a native tribesmen from somewhere in the world, the tribesman had lost the confidence in his religion and committed suicide. his, and our salvation lay, imo, in the surrogate activity of constructing a subjective worldview.
This is a very interesting anecdote (NOT implying doubt, by the way), and you are almost certainly right, even the most primitive of primitives has rudimentary art, rudimentary tattoos (surrogate activiy), and you better believe that creating spears, bows and arrows and other tools was not only necessary for survival long long ago, but ALSO a surrogate activity while simultaneously being a condition sine qua non for survival. Would bet ANYTHING that those anons took great pleasure in all of those activities. 
The depression as a lack of meaning was probably unheard of in those times, except fo the evolutionary dead-end here and there.
